scope: Batch review of R14, A01, A02, A03, A04 only. Files: agent/agent.py (only code file), agent/README.md. Inventory: 2 model calls (agent.py:18 router, agent.py:37 main loop), 0 tool dispatches, 1 audit writer (agent.py:12 record), no queues, no IaC/deploy/CI/identity/recovery code. Prescan: 0 hits. findings.title: Distinct agent identity
findings.requirement: Give the agent its own non-human identity. Keep it separate from the user who launched it and from unrelated agents. Show that permissions and revocation belong to that identity, even when a user starts the run.

not_covered.problem: Action records missing any of the six identity fields
Instance or tenant labels taken from what the model supplies
A credential scoped to more operations, resources, or tenants than needed
Revocation delay from cached or self-contained tokens not measured

checks.check: The agent runs under its own workload principal (service account, IAM role, SPIFFE ID, or agent ID) that no other service or unrelated agent uses.
checks.verify: 1) Find the agent's identity: pod `serviceAccountName`, IAM role, SPIFFE ID, or agent ID in IaC or deploy config. 2) Search other deployments, services, and agents in the repo for the same name or role. 3) Answer no if it is shared, `default`, the main backend's identity, or only a string label with no credential. Answer unknown if identity is assigned outside this repo.
checks.note: agent.py has no deployment, IaC, RBAC, or credential code; client and db are injected by the host (agent.py:17, :30). Searched all of agent/ for serviceAccount, role, token, subject_token, act/sub: nothing. Identity lives outside this repo.

checks.check: Tool and API clients get credentials from the agent's own principal, not from the launching user's forwarded token or session cookie.
checks.verify: 1) Find every place tool and API clients get a token or key. 2) Trace where each comes from: workload identity or token exchange, versus the incoming request's `Authorization` header or session cookie. 3) Check every client, not just the main one. 4) Answer no if any client forwards the user's token or cookie as-is, or uses a shared static key.
checks.note: agent.py has no deployment, IaC, RBAC, or credential code; client and db are injected by the host (agent.py:17, :30). Searched all of agent/ for serviceAccount, role, token, subject_token, act/sub: nothing. Identity lives outside this repo.

checks.check: When a user starts a run, the user is carried as a delegated subject (for example a token exchange with separate act and sub), while the agent keeps its own principal.
checks.verify: 1) Find the code that starts a run for a user. 2) Look for token exchange (RFC 8693, `subject_token`, `actor_token`, `act`/`sub` claims) or a separate delegated-subject field. 3) Check the agent's own principal is still the actor. 4) Answer no if the user's token is used directly or the user replaces the agent identity. Answer unknown if the exchange happens in an outside identity service.
checks.note: agent.py has no deployment, IaC, RBAC, or credential code; client and db are injected by the host (agent.py:17, :30). Searched all of agent/ for serviceAccount, role, token, subject_token, act/sub: nothing. Identity lives outside this repo.

checks.check: Permissions are bound to the agent principal in IaC or RBAC, so revoking that principal alone removes the agent's access without disabling the user.
checks.verify: 1) Find IAM policies, RoleBindings, or grants in Terraform, Helm, or Kubernetes YAML. 2) Check they bind to the agent principal, not to a user, group, or shared role. 3) Check that removing that binding alone would cut the agent's access. 4) Answer no if access depends on the user's grants or a shared credential. Answer unknown if permissions are not defined in this repo.
checks.note: agent.py has no deployment, IaC, RBAC, or credential code; client and db are injected by the host (agent.py:17, :30). Searched all of agent/ for serviceAccount, role, token, subject_token, act/sub: nothing. Identity lives outside this repo.

findings.summary: The repo defines no agent principal, credential source, delegated subject, or permission binding; all are host-supplied.
findings.next_step: Provide IaC/identity config showing a dedicated agent principal, token exchange with separate act/sub, and agent-only revocation.

findings.title: All six identity fields
findings.requirement: Check that every action records the accountable party, operational owner, tenant, agent-type-id, agent-instance-id, and trace context. Look at successful, denied, failed, and background actions, not just the main request path.

not_covered.problem: Identity labels taken from what the model supplies
Agent-type-id not computed as a hash of its identity inputs
Agent able to erase or rewrite its own audit history
Sub-agent record missing its parent link or parent prompt

evidence.note: The only audit writer stores run_id, action, context, result. No accountable party, owner, tenant, agent-type-id, instance-id, or trace context.

checks.verify: 1) Find the audit record schema or the function that writes audit entries. 2) Check for each of the six: accountable party, operational owner, tenant, `agent.type.id`, `agent.instance.id`, trace context (`traceparent` or trace and span IDs). 3) Answer no if any one is missing from the schema or never set.

checks.verify: 1) List every path that writes an audit record, or should: success, policy deny, `except`/`catch` blocks, retries, queue workers, cron jobs, webhooks, other endpoints such as approvals, and refusals before the run starts (quota, rate limit, auth) that return an error without logging. 2) For each, check all six fields are set, ideally by one shared wrapper. 3) Answer no if any deny, error, async, or background path writes records without them, or writes no record at all.

checks.verify: 1) Open the audit record writer. 2) Check it stores trace and span IDs (or `traceparent`) as fields in the record itself. 3) Answer no if trace context exists only in OpenTelemetry spans, or the record's trace field is never filled.

checks.note: No trace_id/span_id/traceparent column or value in the record.

checks.check: Tenant and owner values come from the trusted layer, not from baggage, tracestate, or other unprotected headers.
checks.verify: 1) Find where tenant and owner values for audit records are read. 2) Trace each back to its source: token claims, verified session, IAM tags, or SPIFFE path, versus OTel baggage, `tracestate`, headers like `X-Tenant-Id`, request body, or tool arguments. 3) Answer no if any path takes them from an unprotected source.
checks.note: No tenant or owner is written to records at all. run.tenant is only used for quota keys (agent.py:26); its provenance is host-supplied and not in this repo.

findings.title: Content-derived type identity
findings.requirement: Compute the agent-type-id as a hash of the container digest, harness, system prompt, model ID and version, and configuration. The model part includes checkpoint and fine-tune or adapter references where they apply. Keep the list of inputs (the manifest) and the hashing steps. Check that changing any input changes the ID, and that the same manifest gives the same ID.

not_covered.problem: Changed running config still reporting the old approved ID
Hosted model changing behind a fixed name
Release manifest missing training job, dataset, or model provider records
Action records missing any of the six identity fields

checks.check: The agent-type-id is a hash over a manifest that includes the container digest, harness, system prompt, model ID and version, and configuration.
checks.verify: 1) Find the code or CI step that computes `agent.type.id` (search `sha256`, `hashlib`, `createHash`, `type_id`). 2) List its inputs. 3) Check each is there: container digest, harness, system prompt, model ID and version, configuration. 4) Answer no if the ID is a label, version string, or git tag, or any input is missing.
checks.note: No code in agent/ computes an agent-type-id or manifest (searched sha256, hashlib, type_id, manifest: none). It may be computed in CI or the host outside this repo. Model IDs route-2026-09 and main-2026-09 at agent.py:18,37 are dated names but are not tied to any hash.

checks.check: The hash covers every file that defines the prompt, tools, and configuration, with no file or directory skipped or excluded.
checks.verify: 1) Open the function that lists files to hash. 2) Write down every filter it applies: hidden files, names starting with '_' or '__', extensions, ignore lists, glob patterns. 3) For each filter, check whether a file that defines tools, prompts, or config would be skipped (for example `__init__.py`, `index.ts`, `.env`, `config/*.local.*`). 4) Answer no if any such file is skipped.
checks.note: No code in agent/ computes an agent-type-id or manifest (searched sha256, hashlib, type_id, manifest: none). It may be computed in CI or the host outside this repo. Model IDs route-2026-09 and main-2026-09 at agent.py:18,37 are dated names but are not tied to any hash.

checks.check: The model input is a pinned version or snapshot (plus checkpoint and adapter references where used), not an alias and not the app's release number.
checks.verify: 1) Find the model ID that goes into the manifest or hash. 2) Follow env vars and config to the final value, including defaults such as `getenv('MODEL', ...)`. 3) Answer no if it is an alias (`-latest`, no date or version), falls back to one when unset, or is the app release number. Also no if adapters or checkpoints are used but left out.
checks.note: No code in agent/ computes an agent-type-id or manifest (searched sha256, hashlib, type_id, manifest: none). It may be computed in CI or the host outside this repo. Model IDs route-2026-09 and main-2026-09 at agent.py:18,37 are dated names but are not tied to any hash.

checks.check: The manifest is put in a fixed, documented order before hashing, so the same manifest always gives the same ID.
checks.verify: 1) Open the serialization step before hashing. 2) Check for a fixed order: sorted keys (`sort_keys=True`), sorted file lists, fixed encoding and line endings. 3) Check file lists are not taken straight from directory listing or map iteration order. 4) Answer no if any unsorted dict, map, or filesystem order reaches the hash.
checks.note: No code in agent/ computes an agent-type-id or manifest (searched sha256, hashlib, type_id, manifest: none). It may be computed in CI or the host outside this repo. Model IDs route-2026-09 and main-2026-09 at agent.py:18,37 are dated names but are not tied to any hash.

checks.check: Secret values are not placed in the hashed manifest in a form that exposes them.
checks.verify: 1) List every value fed into the manifest or hash. 2) Check whether any are secrets: API keys, tokens, passwords, private keys, `.env` contents. 3) Answer no if a secret value is written in plain text to the stored manifest, or the whole environment is dumped into it.
checks.note: No code in agent/ computes an agent-type-id or manifest (searched sha256, hashlib, type_id, manifest: none). It may be computed in CI or the host outside this repo. Model IDs route-2026-09 and main-2026-09 at agent.py:18,37 are dated names but are not tied to any hash.

findings.title: Trustworthy attribution
findings.requirement: Assign instance and tenant identity in the trusted execution layer. Don't accept labels the model supplies. Record the delegated subject — the user or system whose authority is being used — separately from the agent's identity. Test that the agent can't pose as another instance or tenant in requests or audit records. Test that trace context survives handoffs between async jobs. Treat trace IDs and caller-supplied labels only as a way to link records. They never prove identity or permission.

not_covered.problem: Agent sharing the launching user's identity
Prompt a parent gave a sub-agent not recorded
Sub-agent authorized using an earlier actor's authority
Action records missing any of the six identity fields

evidence.note: Record schema has no delegated-subject field separate from agent identity.

checks.check: Tenant and instance identity are set by the harness or platform from verified context, never from model-produced text or tool arguments.
checks.verify: 1) Find every place tenant and instance IDs are set for tool calls and records. 2) Check each comes from verified context (token claims, session bound at launch). 3) Check tool JSON schemas the model fills for `tenant_id`, `user_id`, `instance_id`. 4) Answer no if any function uses the model's value, even if another function uses verified context.
checks.note: run.tenant and run.user (agent.py:26) come from the host-supplied run object; verification is outside this repo. No model-fillable tenant/instance field was found.

checks.check: Tenant or instance labels in tool arguments or agent-controlled headers are rejected or overwritten with the verified values before they are used or logged.
checks.verify: 1) Find tool handlers and middleware that receive tool arguments and headers. 2) Check that tenant or instance fields in arguments, or headers like `X-Tenant-Id`, are rejected or overwritten with the verified value before use or logging. 3) Answer no if any handler uses or logs the supplied value, or detects a mismatch and continues.
checks.note: No tool handler or header middleware is in this repo; tool calls are not dispatched here.

checks.check: The delegated subject is recorded separately from the agent identity.
checks.verify: 1) Open the audit record schema and writer. 2) Look for a delegated-subject field (the user or system whose authority is used) separate from the agent principal field. 3) Answer no if only one identity is stored, the user overwrites the agent identity, or the field is never filled.
checks.quote: await db.execute("INSERT INTO events(run_id, action, context, result) VALUES($1,$2,$3,$4)",
checks.note: Record schema has no delegated-subject field separate from agent identity.

checks.check: When work is handed to an async job or queue, the trusted layer attaches the verified attribution and trace context, and the job uses them.
checks.verify: 1) Find queue producers and enqueue calls (Celery, SQS, Pub/Sub, Kafka, cron). 2) Check the trusted layer adds verified identity and trace context to the job. 3) Check the worker uses those values, not ones the agent wrote. 4) Answer no if workers start new traces without parent context or take tenant from agent-written job data.
checks.note: No queue or async job is enqueued here; the handoff in decide() returns text in-process (agent.py:20). Cross-run job handoff is outside this repo.

checks.check: Authorization never treats trace IDs or caller-supplied labels as proof of identity or permission.
checks.verify: 1) Find authorization and permission-lookup code. 2) Check what each decision is keyed on. 3) Answer no if any check uses a trace ID, span ID, correlation ID, request label, or caller-supplied header as identity or to look up permissions.
checks.note: Authorization code is not in this repo; quota keys use run.user/run.tenant (agent.py:26), host-supplied.

findings.title: Recovery integrity
findings.requirement: If logs or checkpoints drive recovery, make them tamper-evident. Before using them, verify them against a separately protected trust anchor or signing key. Test that verification rejects changed checkpoints. It must also catch truncation, rollback to an older valid checkpoint, and replacement of a whole hash chain. For automatic recovery, confirm the destination supports idempotency: sending the same request twice has the effect of sending it once. Replay only within the destination's documented scope and time window. Confirm that actions you can't undo don't happen twice. Where support is missing or the result is unclear, check that replay pauses for reconciliation instead of sending again.

not_covered.problem: What happens to in-flight writes and queued actions at stop
Rollback to an approved earlier release not tested
Agent able to delete or rewrite its own audit history

checks.check: Automatic replay sends idempotency keys that the destination enforces, and only for integrations that support them.
checks.verify: 1) Find replay code. 2) Check it sends idempotency keys (`Idempotency-Key`, `client_token`) only to integrations that enforce them. 3) Answer no if replay sends without keys, uses a local dedupe table as the only guard, or replays to integrations without support.
checks.note: No recovery, checkpoint-load, or replay code in agent/ (searched replay, resume, checkpoint, retry, idempotency, verify, signature: none). events rows at agent.py:13 are plain, but nothing here reads them for recovery; host-side recovery cannot be ruled out.

checks.check: When idempotency is missing or the result is unclear, replay pauses for reconciliation instead of resending.
checks.verify: 1) Find replay handling for unclear results or missing idempotency. 2) Answer no if replay resends instead of pausing for reconciliation, or retry is the default on timeout.
checks.note: No recovery, checkpoint-load, or replay code in agent/ (searched replay, resume, checkpoint, retry, idempotency, verify, signature: none). events rows at agent.py:13 are plain, but nothing here reads them for recovery; host-side recovery cannot be ruled out.

findings.summary: No recovery or replay code is in this repo, so integrity and idempotency cannot be judged.
findings.next_step: Confirm whether the host replays from events; if so show signed/chained records, an external trust anchor and head, and idempotency or reconciliation.
